external.description:
###  After this week’s latest device event from Apple, I’m left with more than one or two thoughts on what was announced.

But before sharing my ‘insights’, a note on the event itself. In days gone by, I’d have been as excited as a puppy, hanging on their every word, and frantically trying to estimate how much I could get for my existing iPhone to justify the upgrade.

Not this time. I’ve adjusted my expectations when it comes to tech companies and no longer enjoy the product launches, self-congratulations and big promises.

As far as I’m concerned, it was an incredibly boring and uninspiring experience until the final “one more thing”. I found myself browsing news sites on my laptop and wandering away from the screen. Frankly, if they somehow managed to bottle the atmosphere, they could sell as it was a cure for insomnia!

Then, the tone changed as they introduced the iPhone Duo. This was really what I’d tuned in for, as I was intrigued as to how they’d pitch it - given all the leaks and rumours about how it was full of compromises.

###  Let me start with the positives.

The iPhone Duo is intriguing and its interface is beautiful. As always, Apple have paid a lot of attention to the little things, down to how the screen changes as you open it, and the fake ‘reflections’ on the bottom screen if you’re watching video on the top.

They’ve managed to include a nice screen, a minimal crease, a great battery and MagSafe charging - all in a relatively small and quite pocketable form factor. Speaking of which, when closed, it reminds me of a time when mobile phones came in a much larger range of shapes and sizes. It’s just a nice break from the same old, same old slabs of glass that absolutely everyone is producing.

I can think of many use cases for this in my own life. Flipping from responding to a message on the small screen, to reading a PDF on the larger screen. From checking the weather on the small screen, to watching a Netflix show on the larger one. Being able to FaceTime hands-free. Fundamentally, it removes the need to carry both an iPhone and my iPad mini.

###  However…

It’s expensive. Even for Apple! Boiling frogs come to mind when I think about apple device pricing. Creeping up and up with a “new normal” each year. Not only the handsets, the price of the cases are astronomical - thankfully, I’m sure the third party suppliers will have some cheaper and more interesting alternatives.

The cameras they’ve included aren’t as good as the iPhone Pro and frankly, my iPhone takes more photos than anything else.

I also have a lot of concerns about durability. It all hinges (pun intended) on foldability, but that fold is going to be used all day, every day. Just how long will it last? The whole phone screams ‘scratch me!’. In Mexico last month, I took my iPhone into the pool with me, left it lying on the granite poolside bar next to my cocktails, and carried it around in my back pocket. There’s no way I’d do that with this device.

So why have a phone if you’re too worried to take it places? Maybe it’s just me, but a case is a non-negotiable purchase. Making the whole thing bigger and heavier.

This got me wondering if that’s why apple have introduced Handoff? A world where people have two different handsets, depending on what they’re doing? I could see how someone would want an iPhone Duo for work activities and then swap over to another iPhone handset when socialising or going to the gym - wherever the big screen isn’t needed.

I don’t think it’s for me, but I will enjoy the in-depth reviews and the real world use in the months following launch. I’ll be keeping an eye on durability, accidents and cost of repair.

Meanwhile, I’ll have several OS updates to navigate on my existing Apple devices. More than enough ‘new stuff’ to play with.

And all completely free.
